results.reason: All fields confirmed against primary text. 14 CCR §27.60(b) lists anchovy as a no-limit species (no bag, no size, no season). §28.90 prohibited-species list (giant sea bass, garibaldi, gulf/broomtail grouper, trout, salmon, broadbill) does not include anchovy, so spear take is OK. §28.80 confirmed for dip net/hoop net. Booklet quote in citation verified verbatim from the 2026 booklet (Regulations Summary Table, updated July 17, 2026). Southern district summary page (updated Sept 1, 2026) has no anchovy row and defers to the general regs. Inseason page: the Sept 11, 2026 domoic acid restriction on recreational anchovy for human consumption applies only from Pigeon Point to Point Lobos (Monterey Bay), not SoCal, as the entry says. Optional wording nit (not a citation risk): §28.80 allows dip nets of ANY size; only baited hoop nets are capped at 36 in. Suggested notes tweak supplied.

corrections.notes: Not counted toward the 20-fish general limit. Dip net any size or baited hoop net up to 36 in allowed (§28.80). Sept 11, 2026 domoic acid restriction (recreational take for human consumption) applies to Monterey Bay (Pigeon Pt-Pt Lobos) only, not SoCal; check Inseason page.

results.evidence: Booklet (https://nrm.dfg.ca.gov/FileHandler.ashx?DocumentID=239985&inline), Regulations Summary Table for Ocean Finfish: "Anchovy, Northern Year Round None None §27.60(b)". 14 CCR §27.60(b) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/14-CCR-27.60): "There is no limit on the following species: anchovy, jacksmelt, topsmelt, Pacific butterfish (pompano), queenfish, sanddabs, skipjack, jack mackerel, Pacific mackerel, Pacific staghorn sculpin, round herring, Pacific sardine, petrale sole and starry flounder." 14 CCR §28.80 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/14-CCR-28.80): "Dip nets of any size and baited hoop nets not greater than 36 inches in diameter may be used to take herring, Pacific staghorn sculpin, shiner perch, true smelt, topsmelt, anchovies, shrimp and squid." 14 CCR §28.90 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/14-CCR-28.90): "Persons who are floating or swimming in the water may use spearfishing gear and skin or SCUBA diving equipment to take fin fish" except giant (black) sea bass, garibaldi, gulf grouper, broomtail grouper, trout, salmon, or broadbill. Inseason page (https://wildlife.ca.gov/Fishing/Ocean/Regulations/Inseason), September 11, 2026: "restriction on the commercial and recreational take of northern anchovy for human consumption" in area "South of Pigeon Point, San Mateo County (37° 11.000' N. lat.) to Point Lobos, Monterey County (36° 31.461' N. lat.)". Southern summary (https://wildlife.ca.gov/Fishing/Ocean/Regulations/Fishing-Map/Southern): "This summary of current regulations was updated on September 1, 2026." — no anchovy row; "See California ocean sport fishing regulations for complete regulations, including regulations for species not covered here".
